scope: Six outcome-specific normative modeling workflows in R

model_comparisons.scope: full healthy-control model and five training folds for all six outcomes
notes: Function environments can differ after runtime isolation; formulas, prior contents, distribution links and model data were compared directly.

Automatic fold creation now drops unused factor levels before assigning groups. Where the old algorithm failed on unused levels, its comparison input was explicitly normalized with droplevels; supplied valid folds were unchanged.

The r4 usability revision retains model definitions, priors, sampling and recovery values. Active configuration defaults were compared; only eight redundant or ineffective continuous-outcome setting declarations were removed.

The r5 readiness revision retains all model definitions, priors and default numerical/sampling values. A-prime prepared model columns, generated and supplied folds, and full/five-fold Stan data were compared exactly against r4; only unused historical audit columns were removed.

checks: available saved synthetic-fit predictions and calibration
all six accepted score tables retain exact score text, participant IDs, row order and public values
long-decimal raw input retains original text through native and shared CSV exports
numerical_and_export_checks.comparison_scope: Model and six completed-export comparisons were performed for r3. The r4 revision compared both changed continuous-outcome scoring wrappers and complete held-out objects with saved synthetic fits. The r5 revision reran all 40 public tests and six check entry points, including shared export checks, and compared A-prime prepared inputs/folds and all six Stan datasets against r4. No new production fits were run. The r6 revision reran all 41 public tests and six check entry points, compared both CSV readers and validated inputs against r5 for all six outcome input files, and verified identical synthetic CSV construction. The strict structure checks do not change valid input values or model calculations. The r7 revision reran 42 public tests and all six check entry points without CPU arguments. All non-resource configuration values were identical to r6. This revision changes concurrency to one worker; it does not change the four sampling chains, iterations, seeds, priors or scoring precision rules. No new production MCMC or fitted-score equivalence claim is made for this revision. The r8 revision updates diagnosis labels to HC/MDD/BD and clarifies the estimated IQ input. All 43 public tests and six no-MCMC check entry points passed with these labels. Numerical preparations, eligibility and row selections were identical to r7 after accounting for diagnosis spelling, and A-prime automatic folds were identical. Numerical model settings and Stan files were unchanged. No new production MCMC or posterior-convergence assessment was performed.

limitations: No new production MCMC fit or posterior-convergence assessment was performed for this reorganization.
Native Windows and macOS execution was not available for testing.
Synthetic checks and preserved model calculations do not establish suitability for a new dataset.
Changed source and output schemas require a fresh output directory; previous caches cannot be resumed.
Prior-predictive check failure policy is unchanged: movement stops, latency records a warning. Inspect all fit and calibration diagnostics.
